content:
As the new school year begins, a growing number of Americans are supporting a full ban on students using phones in class.

With the new school year underway, calls to ban iPhones in schools continue to grow louder.

That's right—although it's only July, summer seems to be ending early. My kids will be going back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive year that the first day of school is no longer in August.

Apple is ushering in the new school year with its annual 'Back to School' promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in participating states can also enjoy a limited-time sales tax holiday.

While the back-to-school deals are exciting, the use of phones in the classroom is increasingly facing a backlash.

Featured comment posted by GreenPizza

I've never seen any data supporting the claim that 'allowing students to use phones during school shootings reduces risk.' In fact, reducing distractions in class is the real key to helping everyone achieve their learning goals.

A recent Pew Research Center survey found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones in class, up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% of people now oppose such bans in schools.

Support for stricter 'all-day bans'—prohibiting students from using phones on campus throughout the entire school day—has grown even more significantly. For the first time, more Americans support an all-day ban than oppose it.

The report also notes that younger adults are less enthusiastic about classroom bans and all-day bans, but since 2024, support has risen across all age groups. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools mandate that students can only use iPhones inside the classroom, implement an all-day ban, or leave it up to students and parents to decide? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
